This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. - `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). - `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52

              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

24	  \]

142	### 4.2 log-softmax 与 f64 累加：16 万宽词表为什么不能用 f32 求和
143	
144	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
145	
146	logprob 的全部数学就是一行：\( \log p_{\text{picked}} = x_{\text{picked}} - \mathrm{LSE}(x) \)。难点全在数值上。
147	
148	三步技巧，每步都有明确理由：
149	
150	1. **max 平移**：先求 \( m = \max_j x_j \)，计算 \( e^{x_j - m} \)。平移后各项 \( \in (0, 1] \)，且至少一项等于 1，因此 \( \text{sum} \in [1, V] \)，\( \ln(\text{sum}) \in [0, \ln V] \)——求和与取对数都落在条件良好的区间，不会上溢（直接算 \( e^{x_j} \)，logit 到 90 就爆 f32 了）也不会全下溢。
151	2. **f64 累加**：求和在 f64 里做。这是本讲的精度核心，下面用误差传播论证。
152	3. **f32 收口**：最终 `log_sum_exp = max + sum.ln() as f32`，回到契约的 f32——损失被压到最后一步的一次舍入里，约 \( 10^{-7} \) 量级，可接受。
153	
154	**f32 累加为什么不行**：顺序累加 N 个正数，每一步加法都可能引入至多 \( \varepsilon \) 的相对舍入，最坏情形总相对误差约 \( (N-1)\varepsilon \)。代入两个数：
155	
156	\[
157	(N-1)\,\varepsilon_{f32} \approx 151{,}936 \times 6\times 10^{-8} \approx 9\times 10^{-3}, \qquad
158	(N-1)\,\varepsilon_{f64} \approx 151{,}936 \times 1.1\times 10^{-16} \approx 1.7\times 10^{-11}
159	\]
160	
161	f32 最坏情形下 sum 的相对误差可达千分之九；误差出现在求和对数里，logprob 直接偏 \( |\ln(1 \pm 0.009)| \approx 0.009 \) nats。即便按随机游走估计 \( \sqrt{N}\varepsilon \approx 390 \times 6\times10^{-8} \approx 2.3\times 10^{-5} \)，也已经和 GPU A/B 测试的对照容差 `TOL = 5e-5`（[tests/gpu_logprobs.rs:L13](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/tests/gpu_logprobs.rs#L13)）同一量级——主机参考实现是全系统的锚点，它自己先抖起来，A/B 对照就失去了意义。f64 累加把这部分压到 \( 10^{-11} \)，彻底出局。
162	
163	顺带一提，源码文档注释用的表述就是这条论证的浓缩版："Exponentials accumulate in f64 — summing a 160k-wide vocab in f32 loses precision"（[src/lib.rs:L468-L469](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L468-L469)）。

165	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
166	
167	```text
168	阶段 1（一遍 O(V)，与 4.3 的 rank 共享）：
169	    max = max_j x_j
170	
171	阶段 2（一遍 O(V)）：
172	    sum = 0 (f64)
173	    for j in 0..V:
174	        sum += f64( exp( f32(x_j − max) ) )     # 平移在 f32 做（输入本来就是 f32/bf16），
175	                                                 # 指数与累加在 f64 做
176	收口：
177	    LSE = f32( max + ln(sum) )
178	    logprob(picked) = x_picked − LSE
179	```

181	注意阶段 2 里 `x − max` 这一步减法留在 f32：两个 f32 的减法自身只有一次 ulp 级舍入，且设备端核做同样的平移，保持两侧一致；**随 V 增长的误差源只有累加**，所以只把累加（和指数）升级到 f64。

253	### 4.3 rank 与 top-k 提取：原始 logit 定名次，插入 + 截断维护前 k
254	
255	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
256	
257	**rank 的时点问题**。rank 定义为 \( |\{\,j : x_j \ge x_{\text{picked}}\,\}| \)。看似可以先算出所有 logprob 再比较 \( \text{lp}_j \ge \text{lp}_{\text{picked}} \)，但源码特意在**减 LSE 之前**、第一遍循环里就用原始 logit 比较，并留下注释 "Rank before subtracting LSE so f32 rounding cannot change raw-logit order"（[src/lib.rs:L497](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L497)）。原因：浮点舍入是单调的，不会把「大于」变「小于」，但**会把「严格小于」塌缩成「相等」**——两个原始 logit 相差比如 \( 10^{-9} \)（f32 已分辨不开），各自减去同一个 f32 的 LSE 再各自舍入，可能落到同一个 f32 值上；此时用 `>=` 比较 logprob 会把那个本应更小的 token 也计入 rank，名次凭空 +1。用原始 logit 比较则不存在这个问题：输入里的相等就是真的相等（bf16 只有 8 位尾数，并列极常见），不等就是真的不等。
258	
259	**top-k 的维护手法**。不求全排序（\( O(V \log V) \) 且要一份索引拷贝），而是维护一个长度至多 k 的降序表，一遍扫描插入：
260	
261	- **快速跳过**：表满且新值 `<=` 表尾（第 k 名）→ 直接 `continue`。真实分布里绝大多数 logit 远低于前 k 名，这个分支消化了几乎全部元素。
262	- **二分定位**：`partition_point` 在降序表上找到第一个「值小于新值」的位置——由于表按值降序、同值按 id 升序，这个位置恰好让新条目排在所有「值 >= 它」的条目**之后**。
263	- **插入 + 截断**：`insert` 后表长最多 k+1，`truncate(k)` 挤掉最小者。
264	
265	**并列的稳定序**。因为外层按 id 从 0 递增遍历，且相等值插入在既有相等值之后，并列 token 在 top 表里天然按 **id 升序**排列。这不是偶然的副作用而是被测试钉死的行为契约（`assert_eq!(ids, vec![1, 4, 2])`——两个并列的 3.0，id 1 排在 id 4 前面）。
266	
267	复杂度：每个未跳过的元素付出 \( O(\log k) \) 的二分加 \( O(k) \) 的插入搬移，整体最坏 \( O(V \cdot k) \)。k 是请求参数（通常个位数到几十），远优于全排序。
268	
269	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
270	
271	```text
272	k = min(top_k, V)                      # k 先夹到词表宽度
273	top = Vec::with_capacity(k + 1)        # 插入+截断最多瞬时到 k+1，预分配避免循环内重分配
274	                                      # 不变量：top 按值降序、同值按 id 升序，长度 <= k
275	
276	for id in 0..V:
277	    val = f32(row[id])
278	    if top.len() == k and val <= top[k-1].值:   # 表满且进不了前 k → 跳过
279	        continue                                #（并列于第 k 名时，先来的 incumbent 留任）
280	    pos = top.partition_point(|(_, kept)| kept >= val)  # 二分：值 >= val 的前缀长度
281	    top.insert(pos, (id, val))                  # 落在所有 >= val（含相等）的条目之后
282	    top.truncate(k)                             # 挤掉最小
283	
284	for 条目 in top: 条目.值 -= LSE                 # 排完序才减 LSE —— 与 rank 同一条纪律
285	```
286	
287	与 rank 的对称性：**排序用原始 logit，报告值最后才减 LSE**。顺序语义（谁进前 k、谁在前）由原始 logit 决定，f32 舍入无从插手；减 LSE 只改变报告的数值，不改变顺序。

330	1. **实践目标**：不运行代码，仅凭源码逻辑手工执行插入 + 截断算法，验证自己对谓词与稳定序的理解。
331	2. **操作步骤**：取行 `[0.5, -1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.5, 3.0]`（六元素，三处并列），`top_k = 3`，`picked = 5`。逐 id 写出每一步 `top` 的内容、跳过分支是否触发、`partition_point` 返回值；最后写出返回的 `top_logprobs`（id 顺序）与 `rank`。再算 `top_k = 6`（k > 并列宽度）与 `top_k = 0` 两种变体。
332	3. **需要观察的现象**：id 3 的 2.0 会插到 id 2 的 2.0 之后而不是之前；id 4 的 0.5 在 k=3 时被跳过（0.5 ≤ 表尾 2.0），在 k=6 时能进表并排在 id 0 的 0.5 之后。
333	4. **预期结果**：k=3 时 ids = `[5, 2, 3]`、rank = 1（3.0 唯一最大）；k=6 时 ids = `[5, 2, 3, 0, 4, 1]`；k=0 时 `top_logprobs` 为空但 rank 仍为 1、logprob 仍等于 \( 3.0 - \mathrm{LSE} \)。可用既有测试 `token_logprob_k_larger_than_vocab`（[src/lib.rs:L680-L693](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L680-L693)）的归一性断言自检：六项 logprob 取指数求和应等于 1。
334	
335	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
336	
337	**练习 1**：跳过条件为什么用 `val <= top[k-1].1` 而不是 `val < top[k-1].1`？
338	
339	**答案**：若用 `<`，表满时与第 k 名**并列**的新值会走插入路径——插到并列者之后再被 `truncate` 挤掉，结果虽然相同（incumbent 留任），却白白付出一次 O(k) 搬移；更重要的是语义显式化：「先到的并列者（id 更小）获胜」。用 `<=` 一行同时买到正确性与快速路径。
340	
341	**练习 2**：`partition_point(|&(_, kept)| kept >= val)` 在表 `[(1, 3.0), (4, 3.0), (2, 2.0)]`、`val = 3.0` 时返回什么？为什么这个返回值恰好保证并列按 id 升序？
342	
343	**答案**：返回 2——前缀 `[(1, 3.0), (4, 3.0)]` 的值都满足 `>= 3.0`，`(2, 2.0)` 不满足。新条目 (5, 3.0) 插到下标 2，落在两个 3.0 之后。因为外层按 id 升序遍历，任何后到的相等值永远插在先到的相等值之后，归纳可得同值组内 id 严格升序。
344	
345	**练习 3**：这个算法最坏时间复杂度是多少？什么时候会真正达到？
346	
347	**答案**：\( O(V \cdot k) \)——V 个元素每个最多一次 \( O(\log k) \) 二分加一次 \( O(k) \) 的 `Vec::insert` 搬移。真正达到要求几乎每个新值都能挤进前 k（比如完全随机的 logits 且 k 较大时）。真实解码步的分布高度尖峰，绝大多数元素命中 `continue` 快速跳过，实际行为接近 \( O(V) \)。
348	
349	## 5. 综合实践
350	
351	把本讲三个模块（泛型输入、LSE 数学、rank/top-k 语义）串成一个任务：**先手算，再写测试钉死**。
352	
353	### 第一步：手算一行 5 个 logit
354	
355	取行 `[-2.0, 0.5, 1.25, -0.75, 1.25]`（五个值全部 bf16 可精确表示，与既有测试的选值纪律一致），`picked = 2`（值 1.25，与 id 4 并列最大），`top_k = 3`。
356	
357	按 4.2 的三步法：max = 1.25；平移后求和（用 f64）：
358

362	| 1 | 0.5 | −0.75 | 0.472367 |
363	| 2 | 1.25 | 0 | 1.0 |
364	| 3 | −0.75 | −2.0 | 0.135335 |
365	| 4 | 1.25 | 0 | 1.0 |
366	
367	\[
368	\text{sum} = 2.646476,\qquad \ln(\text{sum}) = 0.973229,\qquad \mathrm{LSE} = 1.25 + 0.973229 = 2.223229
369	\]
370	
371	于是：
372	
373	- `logprob(picked=2) = 1.25 − 2.223229 = −0.973229`（即概率 \( e^{-0.973229} = 1/2.646476 \approx 0.3779 \)）；

414	## 6. 本讲小结
415	
416	- `token_logprob_from_row` 是 logprob 通道的**主机参考实现**：两遍 O(V) 加一个 O(V·k) 的 top-k 扫描，只在请求方要求 logprob 时运行；它同时是 GPU 批式孪生（u3-l2）的对照标准。
417	- 数学骨架是 log-softmax \( \log p_{picked} = x_{picked} - \mathrm{LSE} \)：max 平移防溢出、把和压进 \([1, V]\)，f64 累加把随词表宽度线性增长的求和误差从最坏 \( \sim 10^{-2} \) 压到 \( \sim 10^{-11} \)。
418	- **顺序语义一律用原始 logit**：rank 在减 LSE 之前计数，top-k 排完序才统一减 LSE——f32 舍入可以把「严格小于」塌缩成「相等」却不能反转大小，用原始值比较让舍入无从制造假并列。

421	- 防御式守卫：空行或 picked 越界返回 `None` 而不是 panic；k 被夹到词表宽度。
422

# token_logprob_from_row：主机端 log-softmax 参考实现

> 本讲属于单元三（logprob 通道），依赖 u1-l1 的分层认知：`pegainfer-sample` 是所有模型 crate 共享的采样策略层，本讲进入它的第二条职责——logprob 提取——的主机侧参考实现。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **推导 log-softmax**：为什么 `logprob(picked) = x_picked − LSE(row)`，其中 LSE（log-sum-exp）要先用最大值平移再求指数和、取对数。
2. **说清精度纪律**：对一个约 16 万宽的词表，为什么指数和必须用 f64 累加，而 f32 累加会损失精度、甚至大到吃掉 GPU 对照测试的容差。
3. **解释 rank 的计算时点**：为什么名次必须在减去 LSE **之前**用原始 logit 比较，而不是比较算出来的 logprob。
4. **读懂 top-k 的维护手法**：插入 + 截断的 O(V·k) 算法、`partition_point` 二分定位、以及并列值按 token id 升序的稳定序是怎么来的。
5. 理解 `T: Copy + Into<f32>` 这一个泛型约束如何让 Qwen 喂 `f32`、Kimi 直接喂 `bf16`，省掉一次 16 万元素的主机加宽拷贝。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲只涉及主机端数学，不需要 CUDA 知识，但需要以下概念：

- **logits**：模型最后一层输出的原始分数向量，长度等于词表大小 V（Qwen3 系为 151,936）。它还不是概率；经 softmax 才变成概率分布。
- **softmax 与 log-softmax**：softmax 把 logits 变成概率 \( p_i = \dfrac{e^{x_i}}{\sum_j e^{x_j}} \)。我们实际要的是它的对数形式（数值上更稳定、也更快）：

  \[
  \log p_i = x_i - \mathrm{LSE}(x), \qquad \mathrm{LSE}(x) = \max_j x_j + \log \sum_j e^{x_j - \max_k x_k}
  \]

  「先用最大值平移」是数值技巧：平移后每个指数项 \( e^{x_j - m} \in (0, 1] \)，且至少有一项等于 1，所以和落在 \([1, V]\) 区间，既不会溢出也不会全下溢。
- **bf16（bfloat16）**：1 位符号 + 8 位指数 + 7 位尾数的半精度浮点。它的指数域与 f32 相同（动态范围一样），但尾数只有 8 位有效位（含隐含位），精度约为 f32 的 \( \frac{1}{256} \)。设备上的 logits arena 就是 bf16。bf16 能被 f32 **无损**表示，所以 `Into<f32>` 对它成立。
- **机器精度（machine epsilon）**：浮点相邻两数的最小相对间隔。\( \varepsilon_{f32} = 2^{-24} \approx 6\times 10^{-8} \)，\( \varepsilon_{f64} = 2^{-53} \approx 1.1\times 10^{-16} \)。把 N 个数顺序累加，最坏情况下相对误差约 \( (N-1)\varepsilon \)——误差会随项数增长，这是本讲的核心动机之一。
- **`Vec::partition_point`**：Rust 标准库方法，在**有序**向量上二分查找「谓词为真的最长前缀」的长度，代价 \( O(\log n) \)。本讲用它维护降序 top-k 表。
- **vLLM 的 rank 约定**：一个 token 的 rank = 词表中 logit **大于等于**它的 token 个数（含并列、含自己），所以 rank ∈ [1, V]。并列最大值的 rank 等于并列的个数。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|------|------|
| [src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs) | 整个 crate 唯一的源文件。本讲主角 `token_logprob_from_row` 在 L473-L520，配三个 CPU 单元测试（L657-L703） |
| [pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/event.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/event.rs) | 契约类型 `TokenLogprob` 的定义处（L3-L9），含 rank 的 vLLM 约定注释 |
| [pegainfer-qwen35/src/logprobs.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/logprobs.rs) | Qwen 侧调用方的快照类型 `LogprobSnapshot = (Vec<f32>, usize)`（L5），证明 f32 喂入路径 |
| [pegainfer-qwen35/src/executor.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/executor.rs) | 真实调用点（L240-L242）：prefill 首 token 的 logprob 计算 |
| [tests/gpu_logprobs.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/tests/gpu_logprobs.rs) | GPU-主机 A/B 测试：把本函数当作设备批式孪生 `token_logprobs_batch` 的对照标准（容差 L13，模型词表 L58-L60） |

> 提示：`pegainfer-sample` 的源码只有一个 `src/lib.rs`（约 700 行），本讲引用行号均出自它，除非另注明 crate。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

回顾 u1-l1 的定位：这个 crate 有两条模型无关职责，`select_batch` 负责「选哪个 token」，logprob 通道负责「这个 token 有多大概率」。logprob 通道有一对孪生实现——设备端批式的 `token_logprobs_batch`（下一讲 u3-l2），和本讲的主机单行参考实现 `token_logprob_from_row`。它是**正确性的锚点**：GPU 测试拿它当对照标准，所以在精度和顺序语义上它必须做到「可解析验证」的严格。

### 4.1 泛型行输入：一份代码同时服务 f32 与 bf16

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`token_logprob_from_row` 接收的是**一整行原始 logits**（不是概率）加上被选中 token 的下标 `picked`，返回契约类型 `TokenLogprob`：

```rust
// pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/event.rs（契约定义）
pub struct TokenLogprob {
    pub logprob: f32,
    /// Count of vocabulary logits >= this token's logit, including ties (vLLM convention).
    pub rank: u32,
    pub top_logprobs: Vec<(u32, f32)>,
}
```

三个字段的语义：`logprob` 是被选 token 的 log-softmax 值；`rank` 是它的名次（vLLM 约定，含并列）；`top_logprobs` 是全词表按 logit 降序的前 k 名 `(token_id, logprob)` 列表。

问题：设备上的 logits 是 bf16，而 Qwen 的执行器在主机上已经持有一份 f32 快照，Kimi 则直接从设备 arena 拷出 bf16 行。如果函数签名写死 `&[f32]`，Kimi 每算一行 logprob 都要先把约 16 万个 bf16 加宽拷贝成 f32——而 logprob 只在**请求方明确要求时**才计算（见函数文档注释 [src/lib.rs:L463-L465](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L463-L465)），为一条偶发路径付一次永久拷贝税很不划算。

解法是一个最小泛型约束 `T: Copy + Into<f32>`：调用方原样交出自己已有的类型，函数在遍历内部逐元素转换。bf16→f32 是无损加宽，语义与先整体拷贝再计算完全一致。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
调用方（两种形态）                     本函数
─────────────────────                ─────────────────────
Qwen: &[f32]（主机快照）  ──┐
Kimi: &[bf16]（设备行）   ──┼──> token_logprob_from_row::<T>(row, picked, top_k)
GPU A/B 测试: &[bf16]     ──┘         │
                                      ├─ 守卫：空行 / picked 越界 → None
                                      ├─ 一遍 O(V)：求 max、累加 rank（4.3 讲）
                                      ├─ 一遍 O(V)：f64 指数和（4.2 讲）
                                      └─ 组装 TokenLogprob
```

两条硬性前置条件（来自文档注释 [src/lib.rs:L466-L472](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L466-L472)）：

1. **行必须是未分片的全词表**：分片局部的 logsumexp 不是全局的，分片调用方必须先跨 rank 归并（#236）。
2. 输入是**原始 logits**，函数内部自己做 softmax 数学。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

函数签名与守卫：

```rust
pub fn token_logprob_from_row<T>(row: &[T], picked: u32, top_k: usize) -> Option<TokenLogprob>
where
    T: Copy + Into<f32>,
{
    let picked = picked as usize;
    if row.is_empty() || picked >= row.len() {
        return None;
    }
```

### 4.2 log-softmax 与 f64 累加：16 万宽词表为什么不能用 f32 求和

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

logprob 的全部数学就是一行：\( \log p_{\text{picked}} = x_{\text{picked}} - \mathrm{LSE}(x) \)。难点全在数值上。

三步技巧，每步都有明确理由：

1. **max 平移**：先求 \( m = \max_j x_j \)，计算 \( e^{x_j - m} \)。平移后各项 \( \in (0, 1] \)，且至少一项等于 1，因此 \( \text{sum} \in [1, V] \)，\( \ln(\text{sum}) \in [0, \ln V] \)——求和与取对数都落在条件良好的区间，不会上溢（直接算 \( e^{x_j} \)，logit 到 90 就爆 f32 了）也不会全下溢。
2. **f64 累加**：求和在 f64 里做。这是本讲的精度核心，下面用误差传播论证。
3. **f32 收口**：最终 `log_sum_exp = max + sum.ln() as f32`，回到契约的 f32——损失被压到最后一步的一次舍入里，约 \( 10^{-7} \) 量级，可接受。

**f32 累加为什么不行**：顺序累加 N 个正数，每一步加法都可能引入至多 \( \varepsilon \) 的相对舍入，最坏情形总相对误差约 \( (N-1)\varepsilon \)。代入两个数：

\[
(N-1)\,\varepsilon_{f32} \approx 151{,}936 \times 6\times 10^{-8} \approx 9\times 10^{-3}, \qquad
(N-1)\,\varepsilon_{f64} \approx 151{,}936 \times 1.1\times 10^{-16} \approx 1.7\times 10^{-11}
\]

f32 最坏情形下 sum 的相对误差可达千分之九；误差出现在求和对数里，logprob 直接偏 \( |\ln(1 \pm 0.009)| \approx 0.009 \) nats。即便按随机游走估计 \( \sqrt{N}\varepsilon \approx 390 \times 6\times10^{-8} \approx 2.3\times 10^{-5} \)，也已经和 GPU A/B 测试的对照容差 `TOL = 5e-5`（[tests/gpu_logprobs.rs:L13](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/tests/gpu_logprobs.rs#L13)）同一量级——主机参考实现是全系统的锚点，它自己先抖起来，A/B 对照就失去了意义。f64 累加把这部分压到 \( 10^{-11} \)，彻底出局。

顺带一提，源码文档注释用的表述就是这条论证的浓缩版："Exponentials accumulate in f64 — summing a 160k-wide vocab in f32 loses precision"（[src/lib.rs:L468-L469](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L468-L469)）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
阶段 1（一遍 O(V)，与 4.3 的 rank 共享）：
    max = max_j x_j

阶段 2（一遍 O(V)）：
    sum = 0 (f64)
    for j in 0..V:
        sum += f64( exp( f32(x_j − max) ) )     # 平移在 f32 做（输入本来就是 f32/bf16），
                                                 # 指数与累加在 f64 做
收口：
    LSE = f32( max + ln(sum) )
    logprob(picked) = x_picked − LSE
```

注意阶段 2 里 `x − max` 这一步减法留在 f32：两个 f32 的减法自身只有一次 ulp 级舍入，且设备端核做同样的平移，保持两侧一致；**随 V 增长的误差源只有累加**，所以只把累加（和指数）升级到 f64。

### 4.3 rank 与 top-k 提取：原始 logit 定名次，插入 + 截断维护前 k

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

**rank 的时点问题**。rank 定义为 \( |\{\,j : x_j \ge x_{\text{picked}}\,\}| \)。看似可以先算出所有 logprob 再比较 \( \text{lp}_j \ge \text{lp}_{\text{picked}} \)，但源码特意在**减 LSE 之前**、第一遍循环里就用原始 logit 比较，并留下注释 "Rank before subtracting LSE so f32 rounding cannot change raw-logit order"（[src/lib.rs:L497](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/src/lib.rs#L497)）。原因：浮点舍入是单调的，不会把「大于」变「小于」，但**会把「严格小于」塌缩成「相等」**——两个原始 logit 相差比如 \( 10^{-9} \)（f32 已分辨不开），各自减去同一个 f32 的 LSE 再各自舍入，可能落到同一个 f32 值上；此时用 `>=` 比较 logprob 会把那个本应更小的 token 也计入 rank，名次凭空 +1。用原始 logit 比较则不存在这个问题：输入里的相等就是真的相等（bf16 只有 8 位尾数，并列极常见），不等就是真的不等。

**top-k 的维护手法**。不求全排序（\( O(V \log V) \) 且要一份索引拷贝），而是维护一个长度至多 k 的降序表，一遍扫描插入：

- **快速跳过**：表满且新值 `<=` 表尾（第 k 名）→ 直接 `continue`。真实分布里绝大多数 logit 远低于前 k 名，这个分支消化了几乎全部元素。
- **二分定位**：`partition_point` 在降序表上找到第一个「值小于新值」的位置——由于表按值降序、同值按 id 升序，这个位置恰好让新条目排在所有「值 >= 它」的条目**之后**。
- **插入 + 截断**：`insert` 后表长最多 k+1，`truncate(k)` 挤掉最小者。

**并列的稳定序**。因为外层按 id 从 0 递增遍历，且相等值插入在既有相等值之后，并列 token 在 top 表里天然按 **id 升序**排列。这不是偶然的副作用而是被测试钉死的行为契约（`assert_eq!(ids, vec![1, 4, 2])`——两个并列的 3.0，id 1 排在 id 4 前面）。

复杂度：每个未跳过的元素付出 \( O(\log k) \) 的二分加 \( O(k) \) 的插入搬移，整体最坏 \( O(V \cdot k) \)。k 是请求参数（通常个位数到几十），远优于全排序。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
k = min(top_k, V)                      # k 先夹到词表宽度
top = Vec::with_capacity(k + 1)        # 插入+截断最多瞬时到 k+1，预分配避免循环内重分配
                                      # 不变量：top 按值降序、同值按 id 升序，长度 <= k

for id in 0..V:
    val = f32(row[id])
    if top.len() == k and val <= top[k-1].值:   # 表满且进不了前 k → 跳过
        continue                                #（并列于第 k 名时，先来的 incumbent 留任）
    pos = top.partition_point(|(_, kept)| kept >= val)  # 二分：值 >= val 的前缀长度
    top.insert(pos, (id, val))                  # 落在所有 >= val（含相等）的条目之后
    top.truncate(k)                             # 挤掉最小

for 条目 in top: 条目.值 -= LSE                 # 排完序才减 LSE —— 与 rank 同一条纪律
```

与 rank 的对称性：**排序用原始 logit，报告值最后才减 LSE**。顺序语义（谁进前 k、谁在前）由原始 logit 决定，f32 舍入无从插手；减 LSE 只改变报告的数值，不改变顺序。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

```rust
// Rank before subtracting LSE so f32 rounding cannot change raw-logit order.
let k = top_k.min(row.len());
let mut top: Vec<(u32, f32)> = Vec::with_capacity(k + 1);
if k > 0 {
    for (id, &v) in row.iter().enumerate() {
        let val: f32 = v.into();
        if top.len() == k && val <= top[k - 1].1 {
            continue;
        }
        let pos = top.partition_point(|&(_, kept)| kept >= val);
        top.insert(pos, (id as u32, val));
        top.truncate(k);
    }
    for entry in &mut top {
        entry.1 -= log_sum_exp;
    }
```

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：跳过条件为什么用 `val <= top[k-1].1` 而不是 `val < top[k-1].1`？

**答案**：若用 `<`，表满时与第 k 名**并列**的新值会走插入路径——插到并列者之后再被 `truncate` 挤掉，结果虽然相同（incumbent 留任），却白白付出一次 O(k) 搬移；更重要的是语义显式化：「先到的并列者（id 更小）获胜」。用 `<=` 一行同时买到正确性与快速路径。

**练习 2**：`partition_point(|&(_, kept)| kept >= val)` 在表 `[(1, 3.0), (4, 3.0), (2, 2.0)]`、`val = 3.0` 时返回什么？为什么这个返回值恰好保证并列按 id 升序？

**练习 3**：这个算法最坏时间复杂度是多少？什么时候会真正达到？

**答案**：\( O(V \cdot k) \)——V 个元素每个最多一次 \( O(\log k) \) 二分加一次 \( O(k) \) 的 `Vec::insert` 搬移。真正达到要求几乎每个新值都能挤进前 k（比如完全随机的 logits 且 k 较大时）。真实解码步的分布高度尖峰，绝大多数元素命中 `continue` 快速跳过，实际行为接近 \( O(V) \)。

把本讲三个模块（泛型输入、LSE 数学、rank/top-k 语义）串成一个任务：**先手算，再写测试钉死**。

### 第一步：手算一行 5 个 logit

取行 `[-2.0, 0.5, 1.25, -0.75, 1.25]`（五个值全部 bf16 可精确表示，与既有测试的选值纪律一致），`picked = 2`（值 1.25，与 id 4 并列最大），`top_k = 3`。

| 1 | 0.5 | −0.75 | 0.472367 |
| 2 | 1.25 | 0 | 1.0 |
| 3 | −0.75 | −2.0 | 0.135335 |
| 4 | 1.25 | 0 | 1.0 |

\[
\text{sum} = 2.646476,\qquad \ln(\text{sum}) = 0.973229,\qquad \mathrm{LSE} = 1.25 + 0.973229 = 2.223229
\]

- `logprob(picked=2) = 1.25 − 2.223229 = −0.973229`（即概率 \( e^{-0.973229} = 1/2.646476 \approx 0.3779 \)）；

## 6. 本讲小结

- `token_logprob_from_row` 是 logprob 通道的**主机参考实现**：两遍 O(V) 加一个 O(V·k) 的 top-k 扫描，只在请求方要求 logprob 时运行；它同时是 GPU 批式孪生（u3-l2）的对照标准。
- 数学骨架是 log-softmax \( \log p_{picked} = x_{picked} - \mathrm{LSE} \)：max 平移防溢出、把和压进 \([1, V]\)，f64 累加把随词表宽度线性增长的求和误差从最坏 \( \sim 10^{-2} \) 压到 \( \sim 10^{-11} \)。
- **顺序语义一律用原始 logit**：rank 在减 LSE 之前计数，top-k 排完序才统一减 LSE——f32 舍入可以把「严格小于」塌缩成「相等」却不能反转大小，用原始值比较让舍入无从制造假并列。
- top-k 用「快速跳过 + partition_point 二分定位 + 插入 + 截断」维护，最坏 \( O(V \cdot k) \)；并列按 token id 升序是被测试钉死的稳定契约（`[1, 4, 2]`）。
- 一个泛型约束 `T: Copy + Into<f32>` 让 Qwen 喂 f32、Kimi 喂 bf16 共用同一入口，省掉 16 万元素的主机加宽拷贝；行必须是**未分片的全词表**（#236）。
- 防御式守卫：空行或 picked 越界返回 `None` 而不是 panic；k 被夹到词表宽度。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

下一讲 **u3-l2「token_logprobs_batch：设备端批量孪生与它的防护栏」**会把本讲的数学搬到 GPU 上：一次 `logprob_topk_batch_bf16_into` launch 处理整批请求，输入三组 i32 缓冲、输出五组缓冲按 `i*k_max + j` 布局回读。带着本讲的三条纪律去读它，你会处处看到对应物——设备核同样按原始 logit 定 rank 与顺序（所以 A/B 的 ids 断言是**精确相等**、数值断言才用 5e-5 容差，见 [tests/gpu_logprobs.rs:L37-L55](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sample/tests/gpu_logprobs.rs#L37-L55)）。建议先通读该测试的 `assert_matches_host`，再进 `token_logprobs_batch`。之后可以延伸阅读 `pegainfer-kernels` 中 `logprob_topk_batch_bf16_into` 的 FFI 定义，看设备端的 f64/归约策略与主机参考如何对齐。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
